citation.title: Image-Based Multiresolution Topology Optimization Using Deep Disjunctive Normal Shape Model
citation.authors: Vahid Keshavarzzadeh, Mitra Alirezaei, Tolga Tasdizen, Robert M. Kirby
citation.version_coded: Abstract only. No full text was reachable: www.sciencedirect.com returned HTTP 403 on every attempt, and no other legal copy exists. Abstract read from the Semantic Scholar API (cross-checked against OpenAlex's title/author metadata).

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: A deep disjunctive normal shape model trained on inexpensive coarse-mesh FE simulation data predicts high-resolution compliance-minimization topologies from simulation parameters; the outputs are described as close to optimal and usable as initial guesses for large-scale optimization, demonstrated on benchmark problems including a 3D case.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No number of any kind appears in the abstract. 'Cost-efficient' and 'inexpensive coarse mesh' are qualitative characterizations of the training-data strategy, not a stated or derivable speed-up factor against a classical optimizer.
claim.alternatives: None identifiable from the abstract alone; the abstract's only other framing is that the predicted designs 'can be used as effective initial guesses for the large-scale optimization problem' - i.e., an accelerator/warm-start role for classical optimization rather than a standalone replacement, which is not itself phrased as a comparison with a number.
